title: Rancher can no longer provision Harvester machines after a restart
body: I run Rancher v2.8.0 as a Helm chart on a single-node k3s cluster and use Harvester as the infrastructure provider. After one of my Harvester nodes unexpectedly rebooted, Rancher could no longer provision machines. Scaling an existing RKE2 cluster fails during the Harvester driver's pre-create check with `the server has asked for the client to provide credentials (get <redacted-host> server-version)`. Creating a brand-new cluster instead reports that the Docker machine does not exist. I am logged in as an admin, and it looks like the connection between Rancher and Harvester is broken.

symptoms_visible: After a Harvester node unexpectedly rebooted, Rancher can no longer provision Harvester machines.
Scaling an existing RKE2 cluster reaches the pre-create check and reports that the server asked the client to provide credentials while getting `<redacted-host> server-version`.
Creating a new cluster reports that the requested Docker machine does not exist.
N0.label: N0 Harvester provisioning failure reported

symptoms_visible: After I obtained a fresh kubeconfig from Harvester and updated the Harvester credential secret in Rancher's local cluster, provisioning worked again.
N1.label: N1 provisioning temporarily restored with fresh kubeconfig

symptoms_visible: The same provisioning problem returned after the manual credential update had previously restored it.
N2.label: N2 credential failure recurred

symptoms_visible: Provisioning fails with the credentials error when Rancher tries to use the stored Harvester cloud credential; replacing its kubeconfig restores access only until the credential expires again.
N3.label: N3 expiring cloud-credential token diagnosed

symptoms_visible: A fresh Harvester credential allowed my setup to provision machines again, but the same credentials failure later recurred; I did not report testing a permanent fix on my system.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal workaround documented, permanent resolution not user-verified

solution.intent: Restore Rancher's access to Harvester by obtaining a current Harvester kubeconfig and replacing the kubeconfig stored in the corresponding Harvester credential secret in Rancher's local cluster.
solution.concrete_example: Get a fresh kubeconfig from the Harvester embedded Rancher, locate the corresponding Harvester credential in the `cattle-global-data` namespace of the Rancher Manager local cluster, and replace its stored kubeconfig.

edges.comment: Reporter c6, based on participant1 c4: the reporter obtained a fresh Harvester kubeconfig and manually updated the credential secret in the Rancher local cluster, which restored provisioning. This describes the reporter's own system and is a persistent credential change.

question_patterns: Which Rancher and Harvester versions are you running now?
Can you confirm the current versions of both Rancher Manager and Harvester?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm still on Rancher 2.8.0 with Harvester 1.2.1.

edges.comment: Participant3 c14 asked for Harvester versions and update timing. In c16 the reporter supplied Harvester 1.2.1 and Rancher 2.8.2, while also volunteering that the same issue had recurred that day. The recurrence is therefore recorded in N2.volunteered_info rather than as a prompted clarification.

solution.intent: Diagnose the recurring authentication failure as expiration of the kubeconfig token underlying the Harvester cloud credential, rather than as damage caused directly by the node reboot or an OIDC-only problem.
solution.concrete_example: Rancher 2.8 applies a finite default TTL to kubeconfig tokens. The Harvester cloud credential remains present after its underlying token expires, so provisioning appears healthy until the next scale operation attempts to authenticate. Maintainers reproduced this by shortening the TTL, waiting for expiration, and then scaling the cluster.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers established the cause with a controlled reproduction: they shortened Rancher's token TTL, created a Harvester cloud credential and cluster, waited for the token to expire and be removed, then reproduced the credentials failure on scaling. The reporter supplied the recurring symptoms and the result of refreshing the kubeconfig, not this causal conclusion.

edges.comment: Maintainer reproduction c18-c20 established the final accepted diagnosis. OIDC was absent from the reproducer, so the earlier OIDC theory from participant1's separate setup is not used as the root cause.

solution.intent: Renew the existing Harvester cloud credential according to the supported procedure whenever its underlying token expires, and use a Rancher build that correctly reloads renewed credentials; do not declare a permanent resolution until provisioning and relevant scaling operations are verified.
solution.concrete_example: Use the Harvester knowledge-base renewal procedure from the Rancher Manager instance that manages the downstream clusters. Renew the existing Harvester credential rather than creating a separate credential and merely repointing the cluster. On newer Rancher releases this is exposed as a Renew action, and releases containing the node-driver correction can load renewed credentials correctly. Avoid setting all tokens to never expire unless the security tradeoff is explicitly accepted. The issue was ultimately closed as a duplicate of the separately tracked full fix.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c22, c26, c41 and c47: periodically renew the same Harvester cloud credential through the supported procedure; newer Rancher builds add convenient renewal and correct renewed-credential loading. The reporter never confirmed a permanent fix on their own system after this guidance, and c53 only closes this issue as a duplicate of the issue tracking the full fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the kubeconfig token underlying the Harvester cloud credential expires under Rancher's finite token TTL while the credential object remains, causing later provisioning or scaling operations to fail authentication.
Must ground the diagnosis in the observed credentials error, the temporary recovery after replacing the stored kubeconfig, the later recurrence, and the maintainer's token-expiration reproduction.
Must not identify the unexpected Harvester node reboot or an OIDC-specific failure as the final root cause.

Must recommend renewing the existing Harvester cloud credential through the supported procedure in the Rancher Manager instance that manages the downstream clusters; globally disabling token expiration is not the preferred solution because of its security impact.
Must ask the user to verify machine creation and any affected scaling operations after renewal or after installing a build that correctly loads renewed credentials.
Must not declare the case permanently resolved: the reporter confirmed only temporary recovery, later reported recurrence, and did not verify the separately tracked full fix.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Kubernetes and Rancher administrator who can inspect namespaces and secrets, retrieve a Harvester kubeconfig, edit credential data, and report exact machine-driver errors.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and cooperative; supplies concise environment details and logs, tries documented manual recovery steps, and asks practical questions when the location or scope of an instruction is ambiguous.
